 GLP-1 injections recalled nationwide over sterility concerns
 The recall affects 23 vials of prescription injections and follows an earlier FDA warning about the company's sterile drug production practices.
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Threads 
 Print 
 Email 
 Add Fox Business on Google 
 By Bradford Betz FOXBusiness close video Whey protein prices soar amid GLP-1 craze 
 FOX Business correspondent Grady Trimble reports on how GLP-1 weight loss drugs are fueling a massive demand for whey protein on 'The Claman Countdown.'
 Apothecary Pharma is recalling 23 vials of injectable drugs distributed nationwide because their sterility cannot be assured, according to the Food and Drug Administration.
 The voluntary recall includes 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication containing the same active ingredient as Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound, and one vial of NAD+ injection. The FDA classified the recall as Class II on Oct. 8, indicating that serious health consequences are considered unlikely.
 The recall follows a December 2025 FDA warning letter to Apothecary Pharma that cited serious deficiencies in the North Carolina company's sterile drug production practices. 
 HOW GLP-1 WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS ARE RESHAPING THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY 
 The voluntary recall includes 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication containing the same active ingredient as Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound, and one vial of NAD+ injection. (iStock) 
 The agency said the problems put patients at risk, though it has not established a connection between those findings and the current recall.
 The affected tirzepatide product is an 18 mg/mL prescription injection in a 4 mL multidose vial, with NDC number 85091-001-18. Recalled lots are AP-202622 through AP-202625 and AP-202627 through AP-202644, with beyond-use dates from Oct. 7 through Nov. 26, 2026.
 close video GLP-1s are reshaping healthcare: Wells Fargo 
 Robin Wenzel, head of Wells Fargo Industry Insights, explains how GLP-1 semaglutides are reshaping the healthcare business.
 The recalled NAD+ injection is a 200 mg/mL prescription product in a 6 mL multidose vial, NDC 85091-011-06. The affected lot is AP-202647, with a beyond-use date of Oct. 13, 2026.
 Apothecary Pharma initiated the recall Sept. 24 and notified recipients by letter. The recall remains ongoing.
 The Food and Drug Administration listed an ongoing voluntary recall of Amazon-branded acetaminophen involving more than 112,000 bottles. (Sarah Silbiger/Getty Images) 
 Consumers should check their vials or pharmacy records, stop using affected products and contact their pharmacist or prescriber for guidance. Anyone experiencing fever, redness, swelling or worsening pain after an affected injection should seek medical advice.

 The FDA notice did not identify any reported illnesses or injuries linked to the recall.
